_comment: Security policy for keel's guard hook. Ships WITH the plugin so it cannot go
missing or drift from the code that reads it — the failure mode of keeping
Patterns are JS regex strings, matched case-insensitively against the Bash
command AFTER heredoc-data removal and env-prefix stripping.
Tiers: blocked = exit 2 (hard stop) | confirm = ask the user | alert = log and allow.
Path globs: `*` matches within one path segment, `**` crosses separators.
Use `**` whenever the intent is 'this directory and everything under it' —
paths.noDelete is enforced for Bash deletion commands only (rm/rmdir/shred/
unlink/srm naming the path, or naming a directory that contains it).
Derived from PAI's patterns.yaml (Daniel Miessler's PAI, MIT), converted

blocked.reason: Recursive delete of filesystem root or home directory
Recursive delete of a critical system directory
Mass delete via find over the filesystem root or home directory
Filesystem format (destroys all data on target)
Raw write to a block device (disk destruction)
Shell redirect overwriting a raw block device
Wipes filesystem signatures from a device

confirm.reason: Piping a remote script directly into a shell (remote code execution)
Reading a secret file and piping it to the network
Copying secrets to a remote host
Force-push rewrites remote history (protect shared and protected remotes)
Uploading a local file over HTTP (possible data exfiltration)
Publishing local content to GitHub (gist/PR) — confirm intended
Netcat/socat to a host (reverse shell / data channel)
Sending command-substituted secret material to a URL (exfiltration)
Installing a third-party Claude skill — review the source before allowing
Renders resolved compose config, interpolating every secret from .env into the output
Dumps the whole environment, including any secrets in it
Prints git config, which commonly carries tokens in remote URLs

Renders or copies private key material — anything read into the transcript is sent to the model provider, and the only undo is rotation. If you did not ask for this, deny. Exits: allow rules in ~/.config/keel/policy.json
Renders or copies credential material into the transcript, which is sent to the model provider. If you did not ask for this, deny. Exits: allow rules in ~/.config/keel/policy.json
